-73.82620,40.75390.name: The New York Fertility Center
-73.82620,40.75390.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Tony Tsai, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-119.81266,39.52618.name: Charles River Laboratories, Inc. - Nevada
-119.81266,39.52618.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-3.50463,51.51250.name: Fertility Home
-3.50463,51.51250.state: 14, Old Field Road, Pencoed, Bridgend, CF35 5LJ
-3.50463,51.51250.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-68.07548,-16.54506.name: Embriovid SRL
-68.07548,-16.54506.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: http://www.embriovid.com/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

101.42991,14.70453.name: Regional Reference Laboratory for FMD in South East Asia National Institute of Animal Health
101.42991,14.70453.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by Department of Livestock Development. It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on animal health. Operational or announced: 2004. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

116.33000,39.94800.name: Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences
116.33000,39.94800.desc: The state agricultural research system, and one of the largest crop research organisations in the world by staff and output. Its gene-editing work in rice, wheat and maize is published in the same journals as everyone else’s, but its priorities are set by national policy rather than by what a market will pay for — which produces a different set of crops and traits from the ones private breeders pursue.

-0.37000,43.32000.name: Euralis / Lidea
-0.37000,43.32000.desc: A French agricultural cooperative with seed and food businesses, operating in a country where growing engineered crops is prohibited and importing engineered feed is routine. Cooperatives sit between the trait owners and the farm and are owned by the farmers, which makes their position on this technology a vote by the people who would plant it.

140.02700,38.72700.name: Spiber
140.02700,38.72700.desc: Ferments engineered microbes to make protein fibres based on spider silk, used in clothing sold by The North Face and others. Structural materials grown in a tank rather than drilled or farmed, and sold to consumers with no label describing how they were made.

-77.02300,38.89450.name: Bee kill incident reporting
-77.02300,38.89450.state: Washington DC — EPA Office of Pesticide Programs
-77.02300,38.89450.desc: A reported bee kill is among the incident types most likely to be investigated, because the loss is visible, datable and belongs to somebody who can be identified. State agriculture departments hold registers of hive locations and can match a kill to applications nearby. For anyone trying to establish what is being sprayed in an area, a hive is both the evidence and the standing.

-95.67520,39.04730.name: In re Syngenta AG MIR162 Corn Litigation
-95.67520,39.04730.state: District of Kansas — federal multidistrict litigation
-95.67520,39.04730.desc: The company was approved to sell the MIR162 trait in the United States in 2010 and began selling it in 2011, before China had approved it for import. In 2013 the trait appeared in shipments to China, China rejected US corn, and prices fell. The farmers who sued had not planted the trait: their claim was that assurances about imminent Chinese approval were false and that the resulting market closure cost them money. Tens of thousands of suits were consolidated in Kansas federal court; a jury awarded about $218 million to some 7,300 growers in 2017; and in December 2018 a settlement of $1.51 billion was approved, described by the lead attorneys as the largest agricultural litigation settlement in United States history, affecting over 600,000 producers, grain handlers and ethanol plants. The company denied wrongdoing throughout and noted the traits were fully approved by all US authorities at launch — which was true, and is the point. Every other case on this map asks whether a release was safe. This one establishes that a release lawful at home can be actionable because another country had not yet approved it.
